items.title: Faerie Hollow Docs
items.text:
Welcome! This is the place to set Faerie Hollow up just the way you like it: every setting, every datapack hook, every sound you can swap, and answers to the questions people ask most.

Looking for something specific?

Press / or S to search every page. Searching a setting's name (like speechBubbles) or a tag (like treats/cat) takes you straight to it.

items.title: Most asked
items.text:
• How do I hide or turn something off? See Hiding and turning things off.
  • Where is the config file? It depends on your loader: see Where the files are.
  • Does it work with Curios, shaders or Sodium? See Compatibility.
  • Something isn't working. Try Troubleshooting, then the FAQ.

items.title: Compatibility
items.text: Mod Status Notes Curios  Supported, optional Adds a satchel slot and a necklace slot. Iris / Oculus with shaderpacks  Supported, optional Tuned for popular packs. Sodium / Embeddium  Works Nothing to set up. Dynamic Trees  Works alongside Faerie Hollow's trees stay its own. Recipe viewers (JEI, EMI, REI)  No special support yet Normal crafting recipes show as usual.

items.title: Curios
items.text:
Faerie Hollow never needs Curios. With it installed, players get:

  • a Familiar Satchel slot in Curios' menu. Each player chooses where to wear their satchel: the built-in slot or the Curios one, one satchel at a time. It works the same in either.
  • a necklace slot (Curios' own kind) for Faerie Favor, which works there just as when carried.

In the Curios slot, Curios' own rules apply: its render toggle hides the satchel on your back, and its keepCurios setting decides whether the satchel drops when you die.

Supported versions: Curios 5.3.0 or newer on 1.20.1, 9.2.0 or newer on 1.21.1.

items.title: For modpack makers
Shaderpacks
items.text:
With a shader loader (Iris on 1.21.1, Oculus on 1.20.1), Faerie Hollow's plants and leaves sway and its lights glow like their vanilla cousins, and the Faerie Realm's sky keeps its pink and purple colors. Glow and light are tuned for:

  • Complementary
  • BSL
  • Bliss
  • Photon
  • MakeUp - Ultra Fast
  • Solas

Other packs work too; these are the ones checked by hand. Without a shader loader, everything draws normally.

items.title: Sodium and Embeddium
items.text: Faerie Hollow works with Sodium (1.21.1) and Embeddium (1.20.1) with nothing to set up, including the realm's colored water.

items.title: Dynamic Trees
items.text: Faerie Hollow's trees are its own whether or not Dynamic Trees is installed: Witch's Willow and faerie saplings grow the mod's own trees, felled and broken as usual. Dynamic Trees only takes over saplings it has a species for, and it has none of Faerie Hollow's.

items.title: Recipe viewers
items.text: There's no special support for JEI, EMI or REI yet. Ordinary crafting, smelting and stonecutting recipes show in them as usual, but Bewitched Cauldron brews don't. In game, the Witch's Grimoire lists every brew the world knows, including those added by datapacks.

items.title: Other mods
items.text:
• Modded mobs can be familiars with a datapack: see Custom familiars.
  • Modded seeds work in Fey Food through the loaders' common seeds tag.
  • Modded biomes can host Faerie Hollow's creatures and structures through tags.

items.text:

items.title: How settings work
items.text:
Faerie Hollow's settings come in two tiers, so the ones most server owners want are never lost among the fine tuning:

File What it holds Who it belongs to faeriehollow-server.toml Start here. The essentials: gathering, speech bubbles, the highest bond level, the realm's portals and foes, foe strength, structures switched off, and percentages that scale whole groups of finer settings at once The world, or the server. In multiplayer, everyone gets the server's values. faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml The bond and its levels, gathering, the satchel, speech, every familiar power and every kind of familiar, bewitched creatures, Whispurrs, the Alraune, Buzzybees and faerie wings The world, or the server faeriehollow-server/creatures.toml Each foe and boss (health, damage, how it fights) and the realm's gentle creatures, mounts and merchants The world, or the server faeriehollow-server/realm.toml The Faerie Portal, everything the realm brings near its players and how often, its doings (faires, bells, wells, bathhouses), tea parties, mushrooms, plants and snow The world, or the server faeriehollow-server/world.toml Which of the realm's structures and features generate, and the mod's loot in vanilla's chests The world, or the server faeriehollow-server/items.toml The Bewitched Cauldron and its brews, the Faerie Altar, the wedding cake, gear, food, trees and faerie houses The world, or the server faeriehollow-client.toml Your own options: music, particles, speech bubbles, accessibility Each player, for themselves.

Every setting is listed, with its default and allowed values, in the settings reference and Client settings and keys. For common changes, copy a ready-made setup.

Percentages stack

A percentage on the front page (like foes.healthPercent) multiplies the matching setting in a topic file (each foe's own healthPercent in creatures.toml). 100 changes nothing, so a file left alone plays exactly as the mod was made.

items.title: World Settings, in game
items.text:
If you host the world (single player, or a world you open to LAN), you can change its server settings without opening a file. While playing, press Esc, then Mods, select Faerie Hollow, press Config, and then World Settings... at the bottom of the screen.

  • Plain controls first. The Foes, Wildlife, Familiars, Whispurrs and Realm tabs cover the changes most players want. Advanced has every server setting, with times given in seconds rather than ticks.
  • For this world alone. What you save is kept in the world's own folder, in faeriehollow/world-settings.json, and goes wherever the world goes. The settings files are left as they are, so your other worlds keep theirs.
  • They win over the files. A setting you change here uses this world's value; every other setting follows the files as usual. Reset Tab, or a setting's own reset button, puts it back to the file's value.
  • Changes apply as soon as you save, for everyone in the world: players on your LAN get them at once. The one exception is the realm's wildlife (how often each creature comes), which changes the next time the world opens; the panel offers to save and quit to the title screen so you can open it again.
  • New Worlds... makes this world's settings the ones worlds you create from now on start with. That choice is kept in the game's config/faeriehollow-new-worlds.json. Worlds you already have keep their own.

Only the host sees it

Players visiting your LAN world, and players on a dedicated server, never see the panel: a server's settings stay in its admin's hands, in the files. A world taken to a dedicated server keeps its own World Settings there, laid over that server's files.

items.title: Where the files are
items.text:
The game makes each file, filled with the defaults, the first time it needs it: the client file when the game first starts with Faerie Hollow, the server files when a world (or server) first starts. The topic files are in a faeriehollow-server folder beside faeriehollow-server.toml.

NeoForge 1.21.1Forge 1.20.1 File Location Server settings config/faeriehollow-server.toml and config/faeriehollow-server/ in your game (or server) folder. Apply to every world. Server settings for one world Copy a file into that world's serverconfig/ folder (a topic file into serverconfig/faeriehollow-server/). That copy then wins for that world. Client settings config/faeriehollow-client.toml File Location Server settings serverconfig/faeriehollow-server.toml and serverconfig/faeriehollow-server/ inside each world's folder (saves/<world>/serverconfig/ in single player, world/serverconfig/ on a server). Each world has its own. Defaults for new worlds Put the files in the game's defaultconfigs/ folder (topic files in defaultconfigs/faeriehollow-server/). New worlds start with a copy of them. Client settings config/faeriehollow-client.toml

In single player

Your world is also a "server", so its server settings work exactly as they do on a dedicated server. On Forge, open the world once so its serverconfig folder is made, then edit the files there.

items.title: Editing the files
items.text:
The files are plain text in the TOML format. Open them in any text editor.

# A line starting with # is a comment, ignored by the game.
[familiars]
    gathering = true
    maxBondLevel = 10
  • Changes apply as soon as you save. You don't need to restart the game or server: the game plays by the new values at once (players' satchel screens may show new level numbers only when they next join). A few settings say they only affect things made from then on, such as new tea parties, new trees, or land generated from then on. How often each of the realm's creatures comes ([spawns.wildCreatures.weights] in realm.toml) is read as the world opens, so it changes the next time the world or server starts.
  • Keep each setting in its [section], in its own file. A setting moved out of its section (or into another file) is treated as unknown and reset.
  • Numbers outside the allowed range are pulled back in. Set maxBondLevel = 500 and the game uses 100, its highest allowed value, and writes that back into the file. A value of the wrong kind (text where a number belongs) goes back to the default.
  • Decimals only where the default has one. Settings whose default has a decimal point (like 12.0) accept decimals; the others expect whole numbers.
  • To reset a file, delete it. The game writes a fresh one with the defaults next time it loads the world.

items.title: Ticks, chances and caps
items.text:
Many settings share the same units:

Ticks The game's clock: 20 ticks = 1 second. So 1200 ticks is a minute and 24000 ticks is a whole Minecraft day. The settings tables show the real time next to each default. Chance (percent) 0 never, 100 every time. Percent (a setting ending in Percent) A multiplier: 100 changes nothing, 200 doubles, 50 halves. enabled Everything the realm brings near its players now and then (goblins, reapers, Whispurrs...) has the same settings in realm.toml: enabled, intervalTicks (how often it has a chance), chance and, where there is one, cap. enabled = false switches one off; hostileSpawns = false on the front page switches every foe off at once. Cap The most there can be near a player at once. When the cap is reached, no more come until some leave. Min and max pairs Familiar settings often come in pairs (radiusMin, radiusMax): the first value is what a familiar has at bond level 1, the second at the highest level, with the levels between scaled evenly.

items.title: For modpack makers
items.text:
To ship your own defaults:

  • NeoForge 1.21.1: include your config/faeriehollow-server.toml and config/faeriehollow-server/ in the pack.
  • Forge 1.20.1: include them as defaultconfigs/faeriehollow-server.toml and defaultconfigs/faeriehollow-server/, so each new world starts with your values. (A file in config/ is not read for server settings on Forge.)

Include only the files and settings you change if you like: anything missing is filled in with its default.

items.title: Client settings and keys
items.text: These belong to you alone: they live on your computer and change nothing for anyone else, even on a server.

items.title: The options screen
items.text:
Press Mods on the title screen, select Faerie Hollow and press Config. Every option in your settings file is there, grouped as it is in the file, each with a note on what it does when you point at it:

Audio The realm's music (on or off, how often it plays, the music of places, caves and nights, the seasons' music, the fight music), and how loud creatures' footsteps and faerie wings are. The seasonal tracks come in the separate Faerie Hollow Seasonal Music resource pack, so without it the realm plays its own music all year. Visuals How many of the mod's own particles you see (falling leaves, sparkles, faerie glitter...), and the realm's snow. Speech bubbles and screen Familiars' speech bubbles (shown or hidden, only your own familiars', their size, how far off and how long they show) and the familiar portraits on satchel icons. Accessibility Reduce flashing: faerie wings about to vanish fade out smoothly instead of flickering. Advanced Performance options, and the shaderpacks the mod adjusts its glow and snow for (editable in the file).

Familiars' chatter plays on the vanilla Voice/Speech volume slider (Options > Music & Sounds), so you can turn it down without touching anything else.

Hosting the world?

Opened from the pause menu in single player or your own LAN world, this screen also has a World Settings... button, for that world's server settings. See World Settings, in game.

items.title: Keybinds
items.text:
Change them in Options > Controls > Key Binds, under Faerie Hollow.

Action Default key What it does Open Worn Familiar Satchel B Opens the satchel you're wearing, from anywhere. Pause or Resume Gathering G Stops your familiar picking up items, and starts it again. Works out in the world, in your inventory and in the satchel's screen. The pause follows you, not the bag: it holds for whichever bag you wear, and is kept when you log out or die.

Note

If the server has switched gathering off for everyone, G only tells you so. Your own pause is remembered for when the server switches it back on.

items.title: The client settings file
items.text: config/faeriehollow-client.toml holds the same options as the screen, for editing by hand or shipping in a modpack.

items.title: [audio]
items.text:
Music and sounds.

Setting Default Allowed What it does realmMusic true true / false Play the Faerie Realm's own music there (its biomes', places', caves' and lullabies). false plays the game's own music in the realm instead. The game's Music volume slider sets how loud either is. musicFrequency NORMAL How often the realm's music plays: the pause between one piece and the next. RARELY doubles it, NORMAL keeps it as made (ten to twenty minutes in a biome, a minute to three in a place), OFTEN halves it, and CONSTANTLY plays each piece straight after the last. Allowed Values: RARELY, NORMAL, OFTEN, CONSTANTLY placeMusic true true / false Play the music of the realm's places (the minotaur ruins, the elves' villages, the grottoes, the faerie hamlets...) while you are in one. false plays the biome's music there. caveMusic true true / false Play the realm's cave music deep under its ground. false plays the biome's music there. lullabies true true / false Play each realm biome's lullaby at night in place of its music. false keeps its own music all night. openingPieces true true / false Play a place's own piece first on coming into it (the Moonspire Peaks' caves, the Crumb Caverns), before its other music. false plays its other music from the first. fightMusic true true / false Play the realm's fight music while a foe is hunting you there, and the Greater Giant's own theme in his fight: it fades in over the realm's music and out again a few seconds after the fight. false keeps the realm's other music playing through every fight. seasonalMusic true true / false Play the realm's Halloween music in the last week of October (25th to 31st) and its Christmas music in the last week and a half of December (21st to 31st), by your computer's calendar, in the stead of its own, when the Faerie Hollow Seasonal Music resource pack is on. false keeps its own music all year. footstepVolumePercent 100 0 to 200 How loud the footsteps of the mod's creatures and of bewitched creatures are, as a percentage of their own (no sound plays louder than the loudest the game plays). 0 silences them. wingSoundVolumePercent 100 0 to 100 How loud faerie wings unfurling, darting and folding are, as a percentage of their own. 0 silences them. wingExpiryChime true true / false A chime as your own faerie wings start to fade, before they wear off. false: no chime.

items.text:

Speech bubbles and what the screen shows.

Raise it to have more time to read them. satchelPortraits true true / false Draw the bonded familiar's head in the corner of a Familiar Satchel's icon. false: the plain bag.

items.text:

items.text: Fine tuning: performance and shaderpacks.

items.title: [advanced.performance]
items.text:
What your computer spends on the mod's renderers.

items.text:
Shaderpack compatibility. Each list names shaderpacks by a word in their names, whatever its case ("solas" matches "Solas Shader v3.8.zip"), so a renamed or forked pack can be added. A change to a list redraws the world's blocks.

items.title: Creature settings
items.text:
Every setting in faeriehollow-server/creatures.toml, in the order it appears in the file. The front page (faeriehollow-server.toml) holds the percentages applied to every foe and boss on top of each one's own here.

When health changes apply

A foe's health follows these settings as it joins the world (spawned, or loaded with its land), keeping the share of its health it had: foes already about keep theirs until then.

items.title: Game rules
items.text:
Faerie Hollow adds no game rules of its own, but it follows these vanilla ones. Change them with /gamerule, as usual.

Game rule What it changes in Faerie Hollow doMobSpawning false stops the creatures the realm brings near players: goblin packs, bombers, reapers, Bedsheet Ghosts, serpents, Whispurrs, brew foes, satyrs and the rest. Not goblin patrols: they follow doPatrolSpawning. doPatrolSpawning false stops goblin patrols setting out (as it stops pillager patrols), and the Satyr Pipers they hire with them. keepInventory true keeps your worn Familiar Satchel (and its familiar) on you when you die. Otherwise it drops with your inventory, familiar safely inside. playersSleepingPercentage Counts players asleep in the overworld and the Faerie Realm together, since they share one night. snowAccumulationHeight How deep the realm's snow and icing can build up. randomTickSpeed How fast an Alraune's garden grows, as for any crop. doMobLoot false stops creatures dropping the mod's loot (such as the Giant's Set). doEntityDrops false stops a broken Faerie Painting dropping itself.

Difficulty matters too

On Peaceful, the realm's monsters (goblins with their patrols and bombers, night reapers, Mandrakes, Puffcaps, Satyr Pipers) and feathered serpents stop coming, and any about vanish; minotaurs never turn on you, and the giants won't wake. Whispurrs, Bedsheet Ghosts, kobolds and the Faerie Faire's visitors still come.

To stop every creature the realm brings, set both doMobSpawning and doPatrolSpawning to false.

items.title: Faerie Realm settings
items.text:
Every setting in faeriehollow-server/realm.toml, in the order it appears in the file. The front page (faeriehollow-server.toml) switches the portal, every hostile spawn and the mushrooms' ward on or off, and scales every spawn's chance.

Every spawn reads alike

Everything the realm brings near its players starts the same way: enabled and intervalTicks (how often it has a chance near each player), then its chances (percent, each time) and caps (the most near a player at once).

items.title: [portal]
items.text:
The Faerie Portal, the way into the realm and back: a Witch's Willow's hollow (switched on or off on the front page).

Players in creative, and any other creature or thing, go at once. searchRadius 64 24 to 128 How far, in blocks each way across, an open portal is looked for where a traveler comes through, before a willow is grown for them with one. A larger search loads more of the world on each trip. nonPlayersTravel true true / false Whether creatures, dropped items and other things that are not players are taken through an open portal. false: only players travel. fromDimensions [] a list The dimensions a portal may be opened in and lead to the realm from, each its id, e.g. "minecraft:overworld". Empty: any. A portal in the realm always leads home to the overworld, whatever this holds.

items.title: Server settings: the front page
items.text:
faeriehollow-server.toml is the place to start: the settings most server owners look for, and the percentages that scale whole groups of finer settings at once (100 changes nothing). To find it, see Where the files are. Changes apply as soon as you save it.

The fine tuning is in the faeriehollow-server folder beside it, one file a subject:

File Covers familiars.toml The bond and its levels, gathering, the satchel, speech, every familiar power and every kind of familiar creatures.toml Each foe and boss, and the realm's gentle creatures, mounts and merchants realm.toml The Faerie Portal, everything the realm brings near its players, its doings, tea parties, mushrooms, plants and snow world.toml Which of the realm's structures and features generate, and the mod's loot in vanilla's chests items.toml The Bewitched Cauldron and its brews, the Faerie Altar, the wedding cake, gear, food and trees

Switching something off

hostileSpawns = false (in [realm] below) stops every foe the realm brings near its players. Each one also has its own enabled in realm.toml. See Ready-made setups for complete examples.

items.title: [familiars]
items.text:
Familiars: the creatures players bond with and carry in a Familiar Satchel (familiars.toml holds the rest).

Setting Default Allowed What it does gathering true true / false Familiars gather loose items for their owners. Each player can pause their own familiar's gathering with a key (G by default); false switches gathering off for everyone, whatever they choose. speechBubbles true true / false Familiars say what is on their mind in speech bubbles, in their own voice: when they are hungry, when their Familiar Satchel is full, when you are hurt, when they are fed or petted, and more. Each player can also hide them for themselves in their own settings. maxBondLevel 10 1 to 100 The highest bond level a familiar reaches. Lowering it never takes affection away: a familiar past it stays at the new top level and has every point back if it is raised again. affectionPercent 100 0 to 1000 How fast every familiar's bond grows, as a percentage of its usual pace (200 is twice as fast, 50 half). powerPercent 100 0 to 1000 How strong every familiar's powers are, as a percentage (150 half as strong again: a wider ward, a longer breath, a likelier find, and waits between uses shortened to match). Each power and each kind of familiar has its own in familiars.toml, applied on top of this. disabledFamiliars [] a list Creatures that may not be bonded as familiars on this server, each its id, e.g. "minecraft:wolf" or "faeriehollow:titania". One already bonded stays in its satchel and can still be released.

items.title: [realm]
items.text:
The Faerie Realm (realm.toml holds the rest).

Setting Default Allowed What it does portals true true / false The Faerie Portal opens and takes travelers to the realm and back. false keeps every portal closed: no one can reach the realm (players already there can still leave through a portal home). hostileSpawns true true / false Foes come near players in the Faerie Realm: goblin packs, patrols and bombers, night reapers, feathered serpents, Mandrakes and Puffcaps, and Satyr Pipers. false stops every one of them, whatever the realm file sets. spawnRatePercent 100 0 to 1000 Scales the chance of everything the realm brings near its players (its foes, Whispurrs, ghosts and satyrs' doings), as a percentage of each spawner's own chance (realm.toml). 0 brings nothing. mushroomWard true true / false Pastel mushrooms (glowcaps), growing or potted, keep monsters from spawning near them, in every dimension (realm.toml sets how near, and in which dimensions). false: they ward nothing.

items.title: [foes]
items.text:
The mod's foes and bosses: goblins, kobolds, minotaurs, brew foes, serpents, night reapers, trolls and giants. Each percentage scales every foe, on top of each foe's own in creatures.toml.

Setting Default Allowed What it does healthPercent 100 1 to 1000 Every foe's health, as a percentage of its own, on top of each foe's own healthPercent. The game holds every creature to 1024 health at most, however high the percentages go. damagePercent 100 0 to 1000 The damage every foe deals, every kind of blow (bites, slings, bolts, tosses), as a percentage of its own. dropsPercent 100 0 to 1000 How much every foe drops when slain, as a percentage (0 drops nothing; past 100, each stack grows to match). experiencePercent 100 0 to 1000 The experience every foe gives when slain, as a percentage. bossHealthPercent 100 1 to 1000 The bosses' (the Greater Giant's) health, as a percentage, on top of healthPercent. The game holds every creature to 1024 health at most, however high the percentages go. bossDamagePercent 100 0 to 1000 The damage the bosses deal, as a percentage, on top of damagePercent. greaterGiantCanWake true true / false The Greater Giant can be woken at Giant's Wake with the Horn of the Old War. false: he sleeps on. bombersBreakBlocks true true / false Goblin bombers' blasts break blocks (only where the mobGriefing gamerule allows it). false: they hurt, but break nothing.

items.title: [world]
items.text:
World generation and loot (world.toml holds the rest). World generation changes apply to land generated from then on.

Setting Default Allowed What it does disabledStructures [] a list Realm structures that no longer generate, each its name as in world.toml's structures section, e.g. "minotaur_ruins" or "goblin_camp". Mind that Giant's Wake ("giants_wake") is where the Greater Giant sleeps and the first source of a Giant's Tooth. crownPiecesInVanillaLoot true true / false Broken Crown Pieces turn up in vanilla's chests and fishing as well as the realm's relic chests.

items.title: [items]
items.text:
Items and blocks (items.toml holds the rest).

Setting Default Allowed What it does weddingCakeFlight true true / false A slice of Faerie Wedding Cake gives faerie wings that fly. false: a slice only slows your fall. pixieDraughtShrinks true true / false The Pixie Draught shrinks whoever drinks it. brewTimePercent 100 1 to 1000 How long the Bewitched Cauldron takes to brew, as a percentage of each brew's own time.

items.title: Ready-made setups
items.text:
Copy a block into the file its title names (where are they?): a block with no title goes in faeriehollow-server.toml, the front page. Replace the lines with the same names, and save. Each setup changes only the lines shown; mix and match as you like.

Every example here is checked

These blocks are tested against the mod's real settings whenever these docs are built, so the names and values are always valid for the current version.

items.title: A cozy, peaceful realm
items.text:
The realm's foes stop coming: no goblin packs, patrols or bombers, no Mandrakes, Puffcaps or Satyr Pipers, no feathered serpents, no night reapers. Whispurrs and the realm's gentle creatures still come.

[realm]
    hostileSpawns = false

Note

Satyr Pipers are foes: at their revels they turn on anyone who steps into the ring, so their doings stop too.

This doesn't cover the realm's folk who live in their own places (minotaurs in their ruins, kobolds in their mines), the Bedsheet Ghosts that drift about ruins by night, or bosses you summon yourself. To stop every creature the realm brings, set the doMobSpawning and doPatrolSpawning game rules to false. Peaceful difficulty stops the monsters only.

items.title: Gentler nights, not none
items.text:
Foes still come, but half as often, and they're a little weaker.

[realm]
    spawnRatePercent = 50

[foes]
    healthPercent = 75
    damagePercent = 75

Or fine-tune each one in realm.toml:

faeriehollow-server/realm.toml
[spawns.goblinCamps]
    followersMax = 2
    refillTicks = 72000

[spawns.goblinPatrols]
    firstDay = 5
    goblinsMax = 3

[spawns.goblinBombers]
    chance = 10
    cap = 1

[spawns.reapers]
    chance = 10
    cap = 1

items.title: A harder realm
items.text:
Foes hit harder and take more to bring down, and the Greater Giant most of all.

[foes]
    healthPercent = 150
    damagePercent = 125
    bossHealthPercent = 150

items.title: Quicker bonds
items.text:
Familiars reach each bond level in about half the time.

[familiars]
    affectionPercent = 200

Or, for finer control, in familiars.toml: less affection needed per level, more for gathering, and familiars hungry for treats more often.

faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[bond]
    curveBase = 10.0
    itemsPerAffectionPoint = 16
    treatCooldownTicks = 3000

items.title: A long-term bond
items.text:
Twice the levels, each taking longer: for servers that play for months. Every perk still runs from level 1 to the highest level, so each level gives a little less, and each familiar power unlocks as far along the bond as before.

[familiars]
    maxBondLevel = 20
    affectionPercent = 67

Tip

Lowering maxBondLevel later never takes affection away: a familiar past the new top level stays at it, and has all its affection back if you raise it again.

items.title: Stronger (or gentler) familiar powers
items.text:
Every familiar power half as strong again: wider wards, longer breath, likelier finds, and waits between uses shortened to match.

[familiars]
    powerPercent = 150

Or only one power, or one kind of familiar, in familiars.toml:

faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[powers.creeperWard]
    powerPercent = 125

[familiars.wolf]
    powerPercent = 75

items.title: Satchels as plain backpacks
items.text:
No gathering for anyone, and every satchel opens all 27 slots from the start.

[familiars]
    gathering = false
faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[satchel]
    slotsMin = 27
    slotsMax = 27

items.title: Quieter familiars
items.text:
Familiars stop chatting in speech bubbles. Or, to keep the chatter but drop the nagging, keep the bubbles and have a hungry familiar mention it only once:

No speech bubblesBubbles, but no repeat reminders 
[familiars]
    speechBubbles = false
faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[speech]
    hungerReminderTicks = 0

Each player can also hide bubbles for themselves, or turn familiars' chatter down on the vanilla Voice/Speech slider: see Client settings.

items.title: No faerie lights
items.text:
Light-giving familiars (faeries, the glow squid, Titania and Oberon, and any custom familiar with the illuminate ability) stop lighting the ground around them as you walk (handy for builders and redstone).

faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[companion]
    faerieLight = false

items.title: Plain trees
items.text:
Witch's Willows and faerie trees grow with plain log branches and no roots, like vanilla trees. Trees already grown keep their shape.

faeriehollow-server/world.toml
[features]
    limbsAndRoots = false

items.title: No goblin camps or minotaur ruins
items.text:
The realm's goblin camps and minotaur ruins stop generating in land generated from then on.

[world]
    disabledStructures = ["goblin_camp", "minotaur_ruins"]

items.title: Lighter on a busy server
items.text:
Fewer creatures kept near each player, a smaller search for an existing portal on each trip (loading less of the world), and familiars gathering a little less often.

faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[gathering]
    fastestIntervalTicks = 10.0
faeriehollow-server/realm.toml
[portal]
    searchRadius = 32

[spawns.whispurrs]
    cap = 1

[spawns.brewFoes]
    puffcapCap = 4

items.title: Whispurrs everywhere they haunt
items.text:
Wild Whispurrs come more often to their ruins, villages and lands, and trust you sooner.

faeriehollow-server/realm.toml
[spawns.whispurrs]
    ruinsChance = 50
    villageChance = 15
    landsChance = 25
faeriehollow-server/familiars.toml
[whispurr]
    trustPlays = 2

items.title: Datapack basics
items.text:
A datapack can change a great deal of Faerie Hollow without touching the mod: where creatures and structures appear, what familiars eat, which mobs can become familiars, what the cauldron brews and what chests hold.

You want to... Use Let a creature spawn in more biomes, or a structure generate in more places Tags Give familiars new treats, or make faeries visit your decorations Tags Make any mob (modded ones too) a familiar, with its own abilities and voice Custom familiars Add your own Bewitched Cauldron brews Cauldron brews Change what chests, fishing and the mod's gifts give Loot Find the mod's structures, biomes and dimension IDs World generation

items.title: Making a datapack
items.text:
1. In your world's folder, open datapacks/ and make a folder for your pack, for example datapacks/my_faerie_tweaks/.

  2. Inside it, make a pack.mcmeta:

    1.21.11.20.1 
    { "pack": { "pack_format": 48, "description": "My Faerie Hollow tweaks" } }

    { "pack": { "pack_format": 15, "description": "My Faerie Hollow tweaks" } }

  3. Add your files under data/, following the paths on these pages.

  4. Run /reload, or restart, depending on what you changed (see below). /datapack list shows whether it loaded.

items.title: The two versions use different folder names
items.text:
Minecraft 1.21 renamed several datapack folders from plural to singular. Use the names for your version:

What 1.21.1 1.20.1 Block tags tags/block/ tags/blocks/ Item tags tags/item/ tags/items/ Entity tags tags/entity_type/ tags/entity_types/ Recipes recipe/ recipes/ Loot tables loot_table/ loot_tables/ Biome and structure tags tags/worldgen/biome/, tags/worldgen/structure/ the same Loader-wide tags c: namespace (data/c/tags/...) forge: namespace (data/forge/tags/...)

One pack for both versions

A pack can hold both sets of folders: each version reads its own and ignores the other's. So neither version calls it a pack for another, give 1.20.1's format as pack_format and list both in supported_formats (which 1.21.1 reads and 1.20.1 ignores):

{ "pack": { "pack_format": 15, "supported_formats": [15, 48], "description": "My Faerie Hollow tweaks" } }

items.title: Adding to a tag, or replacing it
items.text:
A tag file in your pack is merged with the mod's by default, so you only list what you're adding:

data/faeriehollow/tags/worldgen/biome/spawns_faeries.json
{
  "values": [
    "minecraft:flower_forest",
    "minecraft:cherry_grove"
  ]
}

To replace the mod's list entirely (to remove entries, or empty it), add "replace": true:

data/faeriehollow/tags/worldgen/biome/has_structure/goblin_camp.json
{
  "replace": true,
  "values": []
}

For something from another mod that might not be installed, write the entry as { "id": "othermod:thing", "required": false } so the tag still loads without it.

items.title: When changes apply
items.text:
You changed It applies Item, block or entity tags After /reload Custom familiars, cauldron brews, loot tables and loot modifiers After /reload Biome or structure tags (spawns, haunts, music) After restarting the world or server Where structures or ores generate After a restart, and only in land generated from then on

The Tag reference says which applies to each tag.

items.title: Cauldron brews
items.text:
The Bewitched Cauldron's brews are ordinary datapack recipes, so a pack can add new ones or change the mod's own. A brew your pack adds appears in the Witch's Grimoire like any other.

Where it goes: data/<namespace>/recipe/<name>.json on 1.21.1, data/<namespace>/recipes/<name>.json on 1.20.1. Apply changes with /reload.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Two Fey Food from three ingredients, brewed only by night:

1.21.11.20.1 data/my_pack/recipe/moonlit_fey_food.json
{
  "type": "faeriehollow:witch_brewing",
  "ingredients": [
    { "item": "faeriehollow:moonberries" },
    { "item": "minecraft:sugar" },
    { "tag": "c:seeds" }
  ],
  "result": { "id": "faeriehollow:fey_food", "count": 2 },
  "brewing_time": 100,
  "when": "night",
  "color": "#9a7fd1"
}
data/my_pack/recipes/moonlit_fey_food.json
{
  "type": "faeriehollow:witch_brewing",
  "ingredients": [
    { "item": "faeriehollow:moonberries" },
    { "item": "minecraft:sugar" },
    { "tag": "forge:seeds" }
  ],
  "result": { "item": "faeriehollow:fey_food", "count": 2 },
  "brewing_time": 100,
  "when": "night",
  "color": "#9a7fd1"
}

The result is written differently in each version

1.21.1 names the result's item with "id"; 1.20.1 with "item". This follows each Minecraft version's own recipe format.

items.title: Fields
items.text: Field Required Default What it does type yes Always faeriehollow:witch_brewing. ingredients yes Up to six items or tags, in any order. Each goes in once. result yes What the brew makes. brewing_time 100 How long it brews, in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second). when any hour "day" or "night": it only brews then. color "#c79bff" (the cauldron's own violet) The color of the water while it brews, as "#rrggbb". ladled false true for a drink. A ladled brew stands in the cauldron, one serving per measure of water, and each empty glass bottle used on it takes a serving. Its result must then have a count of 1 (one bottle), or the recipe doesn't load.

items.title: How the cauldron chooses
items.text:
• A cauldron brews as soon as its water holds exactly one brew's ingredients.
  • When one brew's ingredients are all part of a bigger brew, the smaller one is made first, unless something only the bigger one takes goes in before. Avoid making a new brew's ingredients a subset of another's, or players may never reach the bigger one.
  • Buckets and bottles only ever fill and empty the cauldron, so no brew can use them as ingredients.

items.title: Custom familiars
items.text:
Any mob, modded ones included, can become a familiar with one JSON file in a datapack.

Where it goes: data/<namespace>/faeriehollow/species/<name>.json (the same path on both versions). Use your own namespace for new familiars. Apply changes with /reload.

To change one of the mod's own familiars, put your file at that familiar's own path, in the faeriehollow namespace, so it replaces the mod's: for the cat, data/faeriehollow/faeriehollow/species/cat.json. A file for the same mob under any other name doesn't replace the mod's; it clashes with it (see When a file is wrong).

items.title: A first example
items.text:
This makes a tamed donkey a familiar that keeps creepers away, fed with treats from a tag of your own:

data/my_pack/faeriehollow/species/donkey.json
{
  "entity": "minecraft:donkey",
  "bond": "owned",
  "treats": "my_pack:donkey_treats",
  "pickup_radius": 1.0,
  "pickup_speed": 1.0,
  "abilities": [
    { "type": "faeriehollow:creeper_ward", "radius": { "min": 6, "max": 16 } }
  ]
}
data/my_pack/tags/item/donkey_treats.json (1.21.1; tags/items/ on 1.20.1)
{ "values": ["minecraft:apple", "minecraft:golden_carrot"] }

items.title: Fields
items.text: Field Required Default What it does entity yes The mob, by ID. A file for a mob from a mod that isn't installed is skipped. bond owned How the player must have won the mob over before bonding (see below). treats none An item tag of the treats it eats. Without one it can't be fed treats. pickup_radius 1.0 Multiplies the gathering reach (0.1 to 10). pickup_speed 1.0 Multiplies how often it gathers (0.1 to 10). affection 1.0 How fast its bond grows (0.1 to 10). 0.25 takes four times as long, as Titania's and Oberon's do. faints false true for a familiar that fights. See below. abilities none A list of abilities. voice its own How it talks in speech bubbles. See Voice.

items.title: Bond types
items.text: bond A player can bond it when... owned they tamed it (cats, wolves, parrots...). trusted it trusts them (a fox trusts only the player who earned it; an ocelot, once trusting, trusts anyone). liked they are its chosen player (allays). rescued it was released from a bucket, by anyone (axolotls). any always: any one of that mob can be bonded.

items.title: Fighters and the rest
items.text: A familiar with "faints": true joins its owner's fights (and only those). It can be hurt, and a blow that would kill it makes it faint and rest in its satchel for a while instead (companion.faintRecoveryTicks in the familiar settings). Every other familiar can't be hurt at all, never attacks anything, and is never attacked.

items.title: Abilities
items.text:
Each ability is an object with a type and its own fields. Most number fields take either a single number, or { "min": a, "max": b }: the first at bond level 1, the second at the highest level, scaled evenly between. A few take a single whole number only, marked whole number below, and unlock_level is one too.

Every ability can also have:

  • unlock_level (1 to 1000, default 1): it only works from that bond level on (shown grayed out in the satchel until then). Its values are then scaled from that level to the highest.
  • hours (any, day or night, default any): it only works in those hours.
Ability type Fields (allowed values, default) What it does faeriehollow:illuminate light (1-15, required) Sheds light where it is, as it goes (the light switched off for everyone by companion.faerieLight = false in familiars.toml; the whole power by powers.illuminate.enabled = false). faeriehollow:creeper_ward radius (1-48 blocks, required) Keeps creepers away from its owner. faeriehollow:guardian radius (1-48, required), damage_bonus (0-100, default 0) Fights for its owner. Only for a familiar that faints. faeriehollow:lookout radius (1-64, required), interval (10-1200 ticks, default 100 → 40) Marks monsters near its owner, so they can be seen coming. faeriehollow:forager chance (0-1, required), loot_table (default faeriehollow:gameplay/familiar_forage) Now and then finds something extra as it gathers. faeriehollow:aquatic regeneration_level (whole number 1-100, default 5), breath (1-100, default 2 → 8) Helps its owner underwater: heals them there, their breath lasts longer, and at a full bond they can breathe water. faeriehollow:tend_growth radius (1-32, required), pulses (1-64, required), name, favors (titania or oberon), bounty (0-1, default 0) Helps plants in #faeriehollow:monarch/tends grow. faeriehollow:court_favour court (titania or oberon, required) Gives its owner the favor of Titania's or Oberon's court. faeriehollow:royal_ward name (required), ward (near or far, required), radius (1-48, required) Monsters near its owner leave them be (near), or monsters far off never notice them (far). faeriehollow:moonpath from (whole number of blocks, default 32) Shows motes leading home once its owner is this far away. faeriehollow:queens_bower none Weaves a bower its owner can sleep in. faeriehollow:love radius (1-32, required), pairs (1-16, required), every (200-72000 ticks, required), crowd (whole number 2-256, default 24) Now and then sets nearby animals breeding. faeriehollow:midas count (1-64 a day, required), gildings (required) Turns items in its owner's inventory to gold once a day. gildings is a list of {"from": item, "to": item, "from_level": level} (from_level a whole number). faeriehollow:lend_wings color (a faerie wings color, required), seconds (whole number 5-3600, default 60), cooldown (whole number 0-86400 seconds, default 300) Lends its owner faerie wings. Outside the realm, below a full bond, they catch the owner's falls for seconds at a time, every cooldown; in the realm, or at a full bond, they last as long as the familiar is out.

items.title: Voice
items.text:
Every field is optional:

"voice": { "lines": "minecraft:cat", "sound": "minecraft:entity.cat.purr", "color": "#E39B4B" }
  • lines: whose speech-bubble lines it says, as an ID. Without it, a familiar says its own mob's lines. Lines are language keys you can add in a resource pack; see Speech bubbles and translations.
  • sound: the sound it makes as it speaks. Without it, its own ambient sound.
  • color: the edge color of its bubbles, as "#RRGGBB".

items.title: When a file is wrong
items.text:
A file with a bad value (an unknown bond, a number out of range, an unknown ability, a malformed color) or a missing required field is skipped as a whole, never half-loaded, and the game log names the file and the problem.

A misspelt field name is not an error: it is ignored and that field keeps its default. If a setting seems to have no effect, check its spelling.

Only one file per mob is used. If two files are for the same mob, which one wins is not predictable (the log warns about it), so to change one of the mod's own familiars always use its exact path. See Troubleshooting.

items.title: Broken Crown Pieces in vanilla loot
items.text:
Broken Crown Pieces turn up in vanilla chests and fishing, added by these loot modifiers:

Modifier Adds a Broken Crown Piece to Chance broken_crown_piece/chests/ancient_city minecraft:chests/ancient_city 0.1074 (about 1 in 9) broken_crown_piece/chests/bastion_hoglin_stable minecraft:chests/bastion_hoglin_stable 0.08 (about 1 in 12) broken_crown_piece/chests/desert_pyramid minecraft:chests/desert_pyramid 0.1566 (about 1 in 6) broken_crown_piece/chests/end_city_treasure minecraft:chests/end_city_treasure 0.0885 (about 1 in 11) broken_crown_piece/chests/jungle_temple minecraft:chests/jungle_temple 0.0857 (about 1 in 12) broken_crown_piece/chests/nether_bridge minecraft:chests/nether_bridge 0.2351 (about 1 in 4) broken_crown_piece/chests/simple_dungeon minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon 0.1862 (about 1 in 5) broken_crown_piece/chests/stronghold_corridor minecraft:chests/stronghold_corridor 0.0165 (about 1 in 61) broken_crown_piece/gameplay/fishing minecraft:gameplay/fishing 0.00556 (about 1 in 180)

Each modifier lives at data/faeriehollow/loot_modifiers/<modifier>.json (the same path on both versions). To change how often a piece turns up, put a copy in your pack with a different chance. To stop it turning up in one place, set that copy's chance to 0. For example, to make pieces far more common in dungeon chests (the mod ships 0.1862):

1.21.1 (NeoForge)1.20.1 (Forge) data/faeriehollow/loot_modifiers/broken_crown_piece/chests/simple_dungeon.json
{
  "type": "faeriehollow:add_item",
  "conditions": [
    { "condition": "neoforge:loot_table_id", "loot_table_id": "minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon" },
    { "condition": "minecraft:random_chance", "chance": 0.5 }
  ],
  "item": "faeriehollow:broken_crown_piece"
}
data/faeriehollow/loot_modifiers/broken_crown_piece/chests/simple_dungeon.json
{
  "type": "faeriehollow:add_item",
  "conditions": [
    { "condition": "forge:loot_table_id", "loot_table_id": "minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon" },
    { "condition": "minecraft:random_chance", "chance": 0.5 }
  ],
  "item": "faeriehollow:broken_crown_piece"
}

A chest gets at most one piece. A piece fished up (in open water only) comes up instead of the catch, and Luck of the Sea doesn't change the odds.

items.title: Tag reference
items.text:
Every tag Faerie Hollow ships, grouped by what it does, with what it holds out of the box. Each is listed by its ID; the file path follows from it. For example #faeriehollow:treats/cat, an item tag, lives at:

  • 1.21.1: data/faeriehollow/tags/item/treats/cat.json
  • 1.20.1: data/faeriehollow/tags/items/treats/cat.json

New to tags? Start with Adding to a tag, or replacing it.

Tip

Use the search (S) with part of a tag's name, like treats or shunned, to jump straight to it.

items.title: Where creatures spawn
items.text:
These biome tags decide where each creature can spawn naturally. Add a biome (yours or another mod's) to let a creature live there too; replace the tag ("replace": true) to move it entirely. Creatures still need the right ground, light and time of day, just as they do in their own biomes. Bewitched creatures (Toadstool Calves, Jackalopes, Truffle Hogs, Hexwool, Mooncalves, Mossbacks, Horned Owls, Grimalkins, Dire Wolves, Blue Moon Hens, Witch's Toads, Hedgefoxes, Blackhorn Goats, Vampire Bats and Hex Newts) are vanilla animals the realm bewitches: they are only bewitched in the realm's own biomes (#faeriehollow:faerie_realm), so a biome added elsewhere gets the plain vanilla animal. Faeries, unicorns and the deer are themselves anywhere.

When changes apply

Changes apply after restarting the world or server.

items.text:
The Witch's Willow is the faeriehollow:witch_willow configured feature, which you can place, or override with a file of your own. Its parts can be used in your own tree features: the faeriehollow:willow_trunk_placer trunk placer, the faeriehollow:cloud_foliage_placer foliage placer, and the faeriehollow:hanging_tresses and faeriehollow:surface_roots tree decorators.

Old names

items.title: What you need
items.text:
Minecraft Loader Lowest loader version Java Curios (optional) 1.20.1 Forge 47.1 17 5.3.0 or newer 1.21.1 NeoForge 21.1.1 21 9.2.0 or newer

Faerie Hollow is one jar per Minecraft version. Use the jar made for your version and loader: the 1.20.1 jar is made for Forge, and the 1.21.1 jar for NeoForge.

items.title: Installing
items.text:
1. Install the loader for your Minecraft version (Forge for 1.20.1, NeoForge for 1.21.1), and run the game once so it makes its folders.
  2. Put the Faerie Hollow jar in your game's mods folder.
  3. Start the game. Faerie Hollow's items appear in the vanilla creative tabs.

Playing on a server?

Faerie Hollow adds blocks, creatures and a dimension, so both the server and every player need it installed, in the same version. See Servers and multiplayer.

items.title: Optional extras
items.text:
None of these are needed. Each adds something when it's there.

Extra What it adds More Curios A Curios slot for the Familiar Satchel, and a necklace slot for Faerie Favor Curios A shader loader (Iris or Oculus) The realm's sky, plants and glowing things are tuned for popular shaderpacks Shaderpacks Faerie Hollow Seasonal Music (a resource pack) Halloween and Christmas music in the realm, in their seasons Seasonal music

items.title: Your first visit to the settings
items.text:
Most players never need to change a thing. When you do:

  • Your own options (seasonal music) are in the mods list: select Faerie Hollow and press Config. Your keys are in Options > Controls > Key Binds, under Faerie Hollow. See Client settings and keys.
  • Everything else (familiars, gathering, the realm's creatures) is a world or server setting. See How settings work.

items.title: Both sides need the mod
items.text: Faerie Hollow adds blocks, items, creatures, a dimension and an inventory slot, so the server and every player must have it installed, in the same version. A player without it can't join. Optional extras (Curios) follow their own rules: Curios also has to be on both sides when it's used.

items.title: Who controls what
items.text: Setting Lives on Who changes it Familiars, gathering, the realm's creatures and dangers, trees, the portal The server (server settings) The server admin. Players get the server's values automatically. A LAN world's host can also change them in game (World Settings). Music, particles, speech bubbles, accessibility Each player's game (client settings) Each player, for themselves. Keybinds Each player's game Each player. Datapacks (tags, custom familiars, brews, loot) The world's datapacks folder The server admin. Resource packs (textures, sounds, speech lines) Each player's game, or the server's resource pack Each player, or the server can offer one.

items.title: Changing settings on a running server
items.text: Edit the server config files and save them. Faerie Hollow picks the new values up straight away, with no restart: the game plays by them at once. The satchel screen's level numbers on players' own screens may only catch up when they next join. See Where the files are.

items.title: Things players share on a server
items.text:
• Familiars are their owner's alone. Other players can't pet, feed, name, lead, ride, saddle, shear or dye someone else's familiar, or take what it holds. They can milk someone's cow, mooshroom or goat familiar.
  • Gathering can be paused per player with a key (G), and switched off for everyone by the admin (gathering = false on the front page).
  • Sleeping counts across the overworld and the Faerie Realm together, by the playersSleepingPercentage game rule. See Game rules.
  • Night visitors come near each player. On a busy server, bombers, reapers, serpents, Whispurrs and brew foes are capped near each player (each spawn's cap), and each goblin camp holds one pack, which a cleared camp gets back only after a day (refillTicks), so ten players in one place don't get ten times the foes. See Faerie Realm settings.

items.title: Updating and moving worlds
items.text:
Back up first

Before any update, of Faerie Hollow, Minecraft or your loader, copy your world folder somewhere safe.

items.title: Moving a world from 1.20.1 to 1.21.1
items.text:
A world made with the Forge 1.20.1 version opens in the NeoForge 1.21.1 version with every Familiar Satchel whole, wherever it is: worn, in an inventory or ender chest, a chest, an item frame or on the ground. Each keeps its items, its familiar (with its bond and affection) and its dye.

One thing doesn't come across: Curios slots. NeoForge can't read the Curios slots Forge saved, so:

  • a satchel worn in the Curios slot comes back in the built-in Familiar Satchel slot instead;
  • any other curios worn in Curios slots are lost. Take them off and put them in a chest before you move the world.

Your server settings come along: on Forge they were in the world's own serverconfig/ folder, and NeoForge treats those files as the world's own copy, ahead of the shared ones in config/. Delete the world's copies if you'd rather it used the shared files. See Where the files are.

items.title: After updating Faerie Hollow
items.text:
• New settings appear by themselves in your config files, at their defaults. Your own values are kept.
  • A setting that was removed is dropped from the file.
  • New structures and ores only appear in land generated after the update. Explore somewhere new to find them.
  • Datapacks you made keep working unless a tag they add to was renamed. Check the Tag reference for the current names.

items.title: Removing optional mods
items.text:
• Curios: take every satchel (and every other curio) out of the Curios slots first, then remove Curios.
  • Shader loaders can be added or removed at any time.

items.title: Setting up
items.text:
Does Faerie Hollow need any other mods?

No. Curios and a shader loader add extras when they're installed, but nothing is required beyond Forge (1.20.1) or NeoForge (1.21.1).

Does it have to be on the server and on every player's game?

Yes, the same version on both. See Servers and multiplayer.

Is there a Fabric or Quilt version?

No. Faerie Hollow is made for Forge 1.20.1 and NeoForge 1.21.1.

Can I use it in my modpack?

Yes, any modpack may include it, public or private, with no need to ask. You may bundle the jar in the pack's download and in its server pack. The one thing to avoid: please don't re-upload the mod on its own or host it on other download sites; send people to its official CurseForge page instead. Faerie Hollow is otherwise "All Rights Reserved".

To ship your own settings with the pack, see For modpack makers.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Where are the config files?

faeriehollow-server.toml (the front page) and the faeriehollow-server folder beside it: in config/ on NeoForge 1.21.1, or in each world's serverconfig/ folder on Forge 1.20.1. See Where the files are.

Do I need to restart after changing a setting?

No. Saved changes apply straight away, on a running server too. The one exception is how often each of the realm's creatures comes ([spawns.wildCreatures.weights]), which changes the next time the world or server starts. See Editing the files.

Can I change settings from inside the game?

Yes, in a world you host. Your own options (music, particles, speech bubbles, accessibility) are on the mods list's Config button, and in single player or your own LAN world the same screen's World Settings... button changes that world's server settings. See World Settings, in game. Players visiting someone else's world, and players on a dedicated server, can't change its settings: those stay in the files, in the admin's hands.

My setting went back to a different number.

It was outside the allowed range, so the game pulled it back to the nearest allowed value. Each setting's range is in the settings reference.

How do I make familiars bond faster (or slower)?

See Quicker bonds and A long-term bond.

How do I stop goblins and other foes coming?

See A cozy, peaceful realm.

items.title: Familiars
items.text:
Can modded mobs be familiars?

Yes, with a small datapack file. See Custom familiars.

Can I give a familiar more treats?

Yes: add items to its treats tag, like #faeriehollow:treats/cat.

What happens to my familiar if I die?

It's safe. Your satchel drops with the rest of your inventory with the familiar packed inside, and a satchel with a familiar never despawns. With keepInventory on, you keep it. If the satchel is destroyed, the familiar is set free where it was.

Can other players take or hurt my familiar?

No. A familiar is its owner's alone, and familiars (apart from fighters, in a fight) can't be hurt. See Things players share on a server.

items.title: The realm and the world
items.text:
How do I find a particular structure?

Use /locate structure with its ID. Every ID is listed in World generation.

Can faeries live in the overworld?

Yes. Add overworld biomes to #faeriehollow:spawns_faeries.

I changed a structure's biomes but nothing changed.

Structures only appear in land generated after the change. Explore somewhere new.

items.title: Looks and sound
items.text:
Which shaderpacks look best?

Faerie Hollow is tuned for Complementary, BSL, Bliss, Photon, MakeUp and Solas. See Shaderpacks.

How do I get the Halloween and Christmas music?

Add the Faerie Hollow Seasonal Music resource pack. See Seasonal music.

How do I hide something?

See Hiding and turning things off.

items.title: Hiding and turning things off
items.text: Everything in Faerie Hollow you can hide, quieten or switch off, and how. For you means it changes only your own game. For everyone means a server or world setting (in single player that's you too).

items.title: On your screen
items.text:
Thing For you For everyone Speech bubbles over familiars Hide them in the options screen (or press F1 to hide the whole interface). Their chatter plays on the Voice/Speech slider. speechBubbles = false in [familiars] on the front page. Hungry reminders repeating hungerReminderTicks = 0 in [speech] of familiars.toml: said once only. The satchel drawn on your back Wear it in the Curios satchel slot and use Curios' render toggle (it hides it from everyone who sees you, not just you). It's also hidden while you're invisible. Familiars' lights (faeries, the glow squid, Titania, Oberon) faerieLight = false in [companion] of familiars.toml. Particles (pom seeds, spores, petals, flakes) Turn down the mod's particles in the options screen, or use a resource pack with transparent particle textures. Flickering faerie wings about to vanish Turn on Reduce flashing in the options screen: they fade out smoothly instead. Tree roots and tapering limbs limbsAndRoots = false in [features] of world.toml. Trees already grown keep their shape.

Can I hide the built-in Familiar Satchel slot?

Not at the moment. The satchel slot next to the player preview in your inventory is always shown, and there is no setting to hide it. With Curios installed you can wear your satchel in a Curios slot instead, and pack makers can remove Faerie Hollow's Curios slots, but the built-in slot stays.

items.title: Sound and music
items.text: Thing For you For everyone Seasonal (Halloween and Christmas) music Turn off the seasons' music in the options screen, or don't install the seasonal pack. Don't offer the seasonal pack. The realm's music Turn it off, or have it play less often, in the options screen; lower the Music slider, or silence a track with a resource pack. Offer a server resource pack that silences it. A particular sound (a creature, an item) Lower its slider (Hostile Creatures, Friendly Creatures...), or silence the event with a resource pack.

items.title: What familiars do
items.text: Thing For you For everyone Gathering items Press G to pause your familiar's gathering, and again to resume. gathering = false in [familiars] on the front page. Picking up particular items Add them to #faeriehollow:familiars_ignore in a datapack. Picking up items you threw away On by default: ignoreOwnerDrops = true in [gathering] of familiars.toml leaves them be. A familiar power enabled = false in its [powers.<power>] section of familiars.toml. Bonding a kind of creature List it in disabledFamiliars in [familiars] on the front page. One already bonded can still be released.

items.title: Creatures and places
items.text: Thing How (for everyone) Every foe the realm brings (goblins, bombers, reapers, serpents, brew foes, satyrs) hostileSpawns = false in [realm] on the front page. See A cozy, peaceful realm. One of them enabled = false in its [spawns.<name>] section of realm.toml. Wild Whispurrs coming by night enabled = false in [spawns.whispurrs] of realm.toml. Satyrs enabled = false in [spawns.satyrs], and satyrHireChance = 0 in [spawns.goblinPatrols] of realm.toml so goblin patrols don't bring them. The way into the realm portals = false in [realm] on the front page. Players already there can still leave. A creature everywhere Empty its spawns_ tag in a datapack ("replace": true, "values": []). See Where creatures spawn. A structure List it in disabledStructures in [world] on the front page. Only affects new land. Every creature the realm brings The doMobSpawning and doPatrolSpawning game rules, both false.

items.title: Still can't find it?
items.text: If what you'd like to hide isn't on this page, it can't be switched off yet. Suggestions for new settings are welcome: they may become options in a future version.

items.title: Known quirks and edge cases
items.text: Things that work as intended but can surprise people.

items.title: Familiars and satchels
items.text:
• Familiars never go through portals themselves. When you change dimension, your familiar is packed into its satchel and comes back out beside you on the other side.
  • Only /kill or the void can kill a familiar that doesn't fight. It then drops nothing and comes back out of its satchel two seconds later. A fighter faints even then (below).
  • A fighter faints instead of dying. It rests in its satchel for a minute (companion.faintRecoveryTicks), and the satchel's tooltip counts down.
  • Closed satchel slots keep their items. If slots close (a familiar is released, or the server lowers satchel.slotsMax in familiars.toml), what's in them stays and can still be taken out, but nothing new goes in.
  • Lowering the highest bond level never takes affection away. A familiar past the new top stays at it, and gets every point back if the level is raised again.
  • Items from dispensers and droppers are gathered, but earn no affection. On 1.21.1, so are items from crafters, vaults and trial spawners.
  • A satchel can't be in two slots at once. With Curios, a player wears one satchel, in either the built-in slot or the Curios slot.

items.title: The Faerie Portal
items.text:
• Players stand in the portal for a moment before being taken (portal.playerDelayTicks in realm.toml); creative players and anything else that steps in go at once.
  • If there's no portal near where you arrive, one is grown for you: a Witch's Willow with its hollow already open, on the most level open ground nearby, never in place of anything built.
  • To go back through, step out first. Having come through, you can't use a portal again until you've stepped out of it for a moment.
  • Open screens close as you go, as with a nether portal.
  • The wither and the ender dragon never go through.
  • Breaking any block of the portal's rim closes it. The trunk is given back as it was.

items.title: Version differences
items.text: 1.20.1 (Forge) 1.21.1 (NeoForge) Server settings files One set per world, in serverconfig/ One set for the game, in config/ (a world may have its own copy) Datapack folders Plural (tags/items, recipes) Singular (tags/item, recipe) Brew recipe result "item": ... "id": ... Datapack painting variants Not possible Possible Gathering from crafters, vaults, trial spawners (not in 1.20.1) Yes

items.title: Multiplayer
items.text:
• The server's settings win. Players can't change familiar, gathering or realm settings for themselves.
  • Other players can milk your cow, mooshroom or goat familiar, but nothing else.
  • Sleeping counts across the overworld and the realm together, by playersSleepingPercentage.

items.title: The game won't start, or says Faerie Hollow is missing something
items.text:
• Check you have the right jar for your loader: the 1.20.1 jar is for Forge, the 1.21.1 jar for NeoForge.
  • Check your loader is new enough: see What you need.
  • If you use Curios, check it's at least the version listed there. An older Curios stops the game loading.

items.title: I can't join a server
items.text: Both sides need Faerie Hollow, in the same version. Compare the version in your mods list with the server's. If the server uses Curios, you need it too.

items.title: My setting changes did nothing
items.text:
1. Is it the right file? Each setting belongs to one file: the front page or one of the topic files in the faeriehollow-server folder. On Forge 1.20.1 each world has its own server settings, inside the world's serverconfig/ folder. On NeoForge 1.21.1, check whether the world has its own copy in serverconfig/: that copy wins over the one in config/. See Where the files are.
  2. Is the setting in its [section]? A setting outside its section is reset. Compare with the settings reference.
  3. Is the value in range? Out-of-range numbers are pulled back to the nearest allowed value.
  4. Does it only affect new things? Some settings (tea parties, trees) only change what's made from then on.
  5. Look in the game log (logs/latest.log) for lines mentioning faeriehollow: the loader reports any value it had to correct.

items.title: A datapack change did nothing
items.text:
1. Run /datapack list and check your pack is listed and enabled.
  2. Check the folder names for your version (tags/item or tags/items...): see The two versions use different folder names.
  3. Check whether the change needs a restart or new land instead of /reload: see When changes apply.
  4. Check the game log for your file's name. A custom familiar with any mistake is skipped whole, and the log says what was wrong.
  5. Check your JSON is valid (a missing comma or quote stops the whole file loading). An online JSON checker helps.

items.title: My familiar won't bond
items.text:
• You must be wearing an empty Familiar Satchel, and sneak + right-click the creature with an empty hand.
  • The creature must be won over: tamed by you (cats, wolves, parrots...), trusting you (foxes, ocelots), released from a bucket (axolotls), and so on.
  • It can't be on someone else's lead, tied to a fence, or ridden by another player. Let it off first.

items.title: My familiar stopped picking things up
items.text:
• Did you press G? It pauses gathering; press it again. The satchel screen's Gathering line says (paused).
  • Is the satchel full? Only its open slots take items; then your inventory.
  • Has the server switched gathering off (gathering.enabled = false)? G then says so.
  • Is the item in #faeriehollow:familiars_ignore, or one you threw away yourself?

items.title: The realm looks wrong with shaders
items.text:
• Update your shaderpack and shader loader.
  • Try one of the packs Faerie Hollow is tuned for.

items.title: Seasonal music doesn't play
items.text:
• The Faerie Hollow Seasonal Music resource pack must be enabled in Options > Resource Packs.
  • Seasonal Realm Music must be on in the options screen.
  • It plays only in its seasons (25 to 31 October, 21 to 31 December), by your computer's date.

items.title: Still stuck?
items.text: Note your Minecraft version, loader version, Faerie Hollow version and other mods, and include your logs/latest.log when you ask for help.

items.title: Resource packs
items.text:
Everything Faerie Hollow shows and plays can be replaced by a resource pack, just as for vanilla: put a file at the same path in your pack and yours is used instead. Everything lives under assets/faeriehollow/.

To change... Look in Block and item textures textures/block/, textures/item/ Creature textures textures/entity/ The satchel and altar screens textures/gui/ (satchel.png, satchel_leather.png, faerie_altar.png, widgets.png) Paintings textures/painting/ Particles (pom seeds, spores, petals, snowflakes, sparkles...) textures/particle/, particles/ Effect icons textures/mob_effect/ Block and item models models/block/, models/item/, blockstates/ Sounds and music sounds/, sounds.json: see Sounds and music What familiars say, and every name and tooltip lang/: see Speech bubbles and translations

Pack format: use pack_format 34 for 1.21.1 and 15 for 1.20.1 in your pack.mcmeta.

items.title: Creatures
items.text:
• Bewitched creatures each have a model file, bewitched/<form>.json, which also holds how they move, and their textures in textures/entity/bewitched/. Replacing a texture is the safe change; a texture must keep its size and layout to fit the model.
  • Elves have one model and texture per look: creature/elf_<look>.json and textures/entity/elf/elf_<look>.png (with an _glow.png for the parts that glow in the dark).
  • Other creatures' models are in creature/.

Glowing parts

An elf's _glow.png is laid over it as light by night (as a spider's eyes are). Keep everything that shouldn't glow fully transparent in it.

items.title: One thing to know about eggs
items.text: Faerie Hollow replaces the vanilla egg item model (assets/minecraft/models/item/egg.json) so Blue Moon Eggs can show their colors. A resource pack that replaces the egg model hides those colors. If you retexture eggs, start from Faerie Hollow's egg model and keep its overrides.

items.title: Sounds and music
items.text:
Replace a sound by adding your own assets/faeriehollow/sounds.json with the events you change, set to "replace": true, and your sound files beside it:

assets/faeriehollow/sounds.json
{
  "item.fey_bell.ring": {
    "replace": true,
    "sounds": ["faeriehollow:item/my_bell"]
  }
}

That plays assets/faeriehollow/sounds/item/my_bell.ogg (an Ogg Vorbis file) whenever the Fey Bell rings. Events you don't list keep the mod's sounds.

To silence an event, replace it with an empty list: "sounds": [].

items.title: Music
items.text:
The realm's music plays on the game's Music volume slider. Each place has its own music event; replace one to put your own track there, or empty it for silence.

For long tracks, mark each sound "stream": true, as vanilla does for music, so the game doesn't load the whole file at once:

  "music.realm.faerie": {

    "sounds": [{ "name": "faeriehollow:music/my_meadow_theme", "stream": true }]
  }
}

items.title: Seasonal music
items.text: The realm's Halloween music (25th to 31st October) and Christmas music (21st to 31st December) come in a resource pack of their own, Faerie Hollow Seasonal Music, kept apart from the mod so the tracks can be full quality. Add it in Options > Resource Packs (one pack works for both Minecraft versions); in their seasons its tracks play instead of the realm's own. Players can still turn them off in the options screen.

items.title: Speech bubbles and translations
items.text: All of Faerie Hollow's text (names, tooltips, the Grimoire's pages and every speech bubble) is in language files, assets/faeriehollow/lang/<language>.json. A resource pack can change any line, or add a language.

items.title: Changing a few lines
items.text:
Your pack only needs the lines you change. Anything you leave out keeps the mod's text.

assets/faeriehollow/lang/en_us.json
{
  "item.faeriehollow.familiar_satchel": "Familiar Backpack",
  "speech.minecraft.cat.hungry.1": "Feed me, mortal."
}

items.title: Speech bubble lines
items.text:
Familiars' lines are numbered keys:

speech.<namespace>.<mob>.<remark>.<number>

For example speech.minecraft.cat.hungry.1, speech.minecraft.cat.hungry.2... Each time, a familiar picks one of the numbered lines at random. Numbers start at 1 and are counted until the first one missing, so leave no gaps: after .1, .2, .3, add .4 (a .5 after a missing .4 is never said). Up to 64 lines per remark.

Remark When it's said hungry It could eat a treat again. bag_full Its satchel's open slots are all in use. fed It was fed a treat or Fey Food. petted Its owner petted it. level_up Its bond grew a level. bonded It has just become its owner's familiar. sleepy Its owner lay down to sleep. worried Its owner is badly hurt. debuffed Fighters only: something harmful was put on it (poison, weakness...). hurt Fighters only: it is badly hurt. recovered Fighters only: it is back after fainting. dancing Faeries: given their favorite treat. gathered Faeries: picked something up (once in a long while). crown, queen, king Faeries: shown a piece of a fallen monarch's crown, or a shard of the Moon or Sun. royal_crown, own_shard, mourn_queen, mourn_king Titania and Oberon: shown their own relics, or their consort's.

A remark a familiar has no lines for is said with the shared lines in speech.faeriehollow.familiar.<remark>.<number>.

Lines for a modded creature

A custom familiar says its own mob's lines, so a familiar made from othermod:otter reads speech.othermod.otter.hungry.1 and so on. Add them in a resource pack's language file, or point its voice.lines at another mob's lines.

items.title: Translating
items.text:
Faerie Hollow is already translated into 13 languages. To add another, or improve one:

  1. Copy the English file, assets/faeriehollow/lang/en_us.json (from the mod's jar), to your language's code, for example nl_nl.json, in a resource pack.
  2. Translate the text on the right of each line. Leave the keys on the left as they are.
  3. Keep every %s: the game fills them in with names and numbers, in order. If your sentence needs them in another order, number them: %2$s ... %1$s.
  4. Use your language's own Minecraft words (for "spawn egg", "sneak", "inventory"...) so it reads like the rest of the game.
